target.urlHint: On a host rvav may call, as Integrations sets
target.awxHint: It gets the event as the extra variable rvav_event.

topicGroups.machine: A request's VMs, one event each
topicGroups.custom: A request's custom resources, one event each

changes.name: the VM's name (machine.name)
changes.placement: its cluster, resource pool, datastore and folder (machine.placement)

run.title: Run
run.recoveryOf: Its recovery target, after the subscription failed
run.noAnswer: None: the subscription's setting for when it fails decided

runs.title: Runs
runs.lead: One for each event it heard about. Open one to see what was sent and what came back.
runs.noneBody: It runs for each event that matches. To see one now, send it a test event from the menu above.
runs.noneWithBody: Other runs may have another status.

sheet.lead: What it hears about, and what is told.
sheet.conditionHint: Over the event's data; empty for every event. For example environment == "prd" && item.slug == "rhel9-server"
sheet.blocking: Blocking: the request waits for the answer, which may stop it
sheet.mayChange: Its answer may also change {{changes}}; rvav checks the change again before building, as it checked the request.
sheet.answers: A webhook answers with JSON, an AWX job with the rvav_answer artifact (set_stats), a custom workflow with its result.
sheet.onFailure: When it fails, doesn't answer or asks for a change rvav refuses
sheet.recovers: Tell a recovery target when it fails
sheet.recoveryLead: Told once, with the event and why it failed (recovery.reason). If it answers stop or continue, that decides; otherwise the setting above does.

remove.body: Its runs, with what each sent and got back, go with it. To keep them, turn it off instead.
remove.blocking: Requests stop waiting for its answer on {{topic}}.

subscriptions.lead: Webhooks, AWX templates and custom workflows that hear about requests, their approvals, each VM a request builds or deletes, day-2 actions, leases and projects. A blocking one may stop a request.
subscriptions.label: Subscriptions
subscriptions.noneBody: Subscribe a webhook, an AWX template or a custom workflow to a topic, such as a VM built, to tell another system.

subscription.title: Subscription
subscription.blockingStops: Yes: the request stops when it fails, doesn't answer or asks for a change rvav refuses
subscription.blockingGoesOn: Yes: the request goes on when it fails, doesn't answer or asks for a change rvav refuses

sheet.lead: Blueprints and composite steps make its resources; deployments show them like VMs, and deleting a deployment deletes them.
sheet.lifeLead: A custom workflow registered for resource types gets the resource's inputs and returns its properties; an AWX template gets them as extra variables and returns them with set_stats.
sheet.schemaHint: What it returns: later steps read these properties, and the deployment page shows them by their titles.
sheet.noActions: No custom workflow is registered as a day-2 action, and AWX offers none.

resourceTypes.lead: What rvav doesn't build itself, such as load balancers: a custom workflow or an AWX template creates each resource, and another deletes it. Blueprints and composite steps use them.
resourceTypes.label: Resource types
resourceTypes.noneBody: Define one to let blueprints make what rvav doesn't build itself, with your workflows or AWX templates.

remove.body: Blueprints and composite steps can no longer use it.
remove.consequences: rvav forgets the type. Its custom workflows and AWX templates aren't changed.

sheet.lead: Its own workers run it in Temporal; rvav starts it with the form its input schema describes.
sheet.typeHint: Ends with its major version: decommission.v1
sheet.schemaHint: The form people fill when they start it.
sheet.projectsLead: None ticked: every project may use it.

workflows.lead: Temporal workflows your teams write, run by their own workers; rvav starts them, shows their steps and asks for their approvals.
workflows.noneBody: Add one to offer it in the catalog, on deployments or to subscriptions.

remove.body: rvav forgets its registration: it no longer starts it. Its workers and Temporal aren't changed.
remove.consequences: It is no longer offered as {{usages}}. If requests ran it, it is refused: turn it off instead.
